guard: a bearer source returning a token already inside its refresh margin is refused, so BEARER_RETRY_MS applies instead of the 5s floor
why: Adopting a token already inside its own refresh margin arms the next refresh from a non-positive
delay, which armBearerRefresh floors to 5s. The next read returns the same near-dead token, so the
loop runs at 5s for its remaining life while the 15s BEARER_RETRY_MS backoff is bypassed: the fetch
did not fail, it succeeded and returned material that is not usable.
The named cell counts source reads in a window longer than the 5s floor and shorter than the 15s
backoff, so it grades the loop itself rather than the message. The sibling cells - the warning text
and the cache staying on the last good token - cannot grade it alone: a future change could emit
that message, or leave the cache alone, and still re-read at the floor.

This fixture cannot tell the narrowed rule from the original one: its stale token does not advance the expiry, so BOTH rules refuse it. What tells them apart is `smoke:expiry-renewal:auth`, which mints 5s bearers against the 60s margin — the original rule turned that suite red, the narrowed one leaves it green. The pair is the evidence, not a mutation here.

mutations.name: a non-advancing token is adopted instead of refused
mutations.expectRed: the refusal backs off past the 5s floor (no re-read in 12s)
mutations.cell: the refusal backs off past the 5s floor (no re-read in 12s)
mutations.note: Flipping the advance test, not deleting the guard: a deleted guard also reds the cell, but so would any change that stops the refusal firing. Inverting it keeps the refusal armed for exactly the tokens that ARE fresh — the shape `expiry-renewal` depends on — so the cell fails if the rule ever goes back to refusing a short lifetime.
